# SOP: Automated Transport Purchase Orders and Route Classification

**Document purpose:** This procedure explains every Stage 1 transport purchase-order (PO) type generated by the AP Invoice Manager’s Vtiger-to-Xero automation. It gives operations and accounts staff a consistent way to identify the correct PO prefix, with particular attention to movements **from** and **to** rail yards.

**Scope:** The procedure covers only the POs created when a Vtiger Stage 1 webhook contains a recognised, non-zero transport-cost field. It does not create POs merely because a job exists or a deal number is present. A zero or blank cost field is not converted into a PO. [1]

> **Core rule:** Classify the *physical transport leg*, not the invoice wording. First determine whether the container is empty or full, then identify whether the leg starts at a customer/origin, a rail terminal/yard, a depot, a storage site, or the final destination.

## 1. How the automation creates a PO

The automation receives a Stage 1 Vtiger webhook. For every recognised cost field that contains a non-zero amount, it creates one Xero **Draft** PO. Each PO uses account code **310**, is sent as **GST-exclusive** with **INPUT** tax treatment, and uses the configured supplier or the approved Containerzone fallback where an external supplier cannot be safely resolved. Before creating a PO, it checks whether the same PO number already exists in Xero; an existing PO is recorded as a duplicate rather than being created again. [1]

| Decision point | Operational consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Recognised cost field has a positive value | Create one draft PO for that transport or related cost leg. |
| Cost field is blank, zero, or non-numeric | Do not create a PO for that leg; it is recorded as skipped. |
| Webhook contains only a deal number and no recognised cost fields | No PO can be created; the workflow is recorded as failed with a clear reason. |
| Same calculated PO number already exists in Xero | Do not create a second PO; review the existing PO before taking further action. |
| Several recognised cost fields are non-zero | Create one PO for each applicable leg/cost. A single deal can therefore produce multiple POs. |

## 2. Reading an automated PO number

Most road-transport POs follow this pattern:

> **`[Prefix]D[Deal digits]`**

For example, Vtiger deal **`D702837`** produces `AD702837`, `BD702837`, `DD702837`, and `ED702837` when the corresponding costs are supplied. The `D` after the prefix is part of the standard road-transport PO format; the deal’s leading `D` is not duplicated.

| Example input deal | Prefix | Generated PO | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D702837` | `A` | `AD702837` | Empty container delivery. |
| `D702837` | `B` | `BD702837` | Full container collection. |
| `D702837` | `D` | `DD702837` | Full container delivery. |
| `D702837` | `E` | `ED702837` | Empty container dehire/return. |

Some rail and specialised movements deliberately omit the inserted `D`, and Hub Transfer 2 has a suffix. These exceptions are listed in Section 5. [1]

## 3. The four main route PO types: AD, BD, DD and ED

The following table is the primary operating reference. The columns **“from”** and **“to”** refer to the real transport leg, not simply the broad job origin and destination recorded on the deal.

| PO | Container state on the leg | Route classification | Typical **from** location | Typical **to** location | Rail-yard test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **AD** | Empty | Empty container delivery | Empty depot, container yard, or a rail-terminal empty release point | Packer, exporter, customer origin, or loading site | A rail yard can be the **starting point** only when the empty container is released there. The movement is **not** a delivery to the rail yard. |
| **BD** | Full | Full container collection | Packer, exporter, customer origin, or loaded collection site | Rail yard, rail terminal, port terminal, or nominated line-haul handover point | This is the principal **to-the-rail-yard** PO. If the full container is collected from the customer and delivered into rail, use BD. |
| **DD** | Full | Full container delivery | Rail yard, rail terminal, port terminal, staging point, or other nominated full-container handover location | Consignee, customer delivery site, or final destination | This is the principal **from-the-rail-yard** PO. If the full container leaves rail for the customer, use DD. |
| **ED** | Empty | Empty dehire / empty return | Consignee, unpacking site, customer delivery site, or empty release point after unloading | Dehire depot, empty container depot, nominated return yard, or reseller location | A rail yard is not assumed. Use ED only for the empty post-unpack return leg; if a rail yard is the nominated return location, it is the **destination**. |

### 3.1 AD — Empty Container Delivery: `AD[deal]`

Use **AD** when an **empty** container is being moved **to the loading/origin side** of the job. The empty container normally starts at an empty depot or container yard and is taken to the exporter, packer, customer, or other site where it will be loaded.

The key question is: **“Is the container empty and being delivered to the place where cargo will be loaded?”** If yes, it is an AD leg. If the empty container is released from a rail-yard facility, the rail yard is the *from* location; the route remains AD because the container is empty and the destination is the origin/loading site.

| AD example | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| `D702837 EMPTY 20ft from Dynon empty release to Laverton packing site` | `AD702837` — empty container leaves the yard/depot and is delivered to the packing origin. |
| `D702837 EMPTY 40ft from rail terminal empty stack to Dandenong exporter` | `AD702837` — rail terminal is the starting point, but the movement is still an empty delivery. |
| `D702837 loaded container from Laverton to Dynon terminal` | **Not AD**; this is BD because the container is full and is travelling to rail. |

### 3.2 BD — Full Container Collection: `BD[deal]`

Use **BD** when a **full** container is collected from the origin/packing location and transported **to a rail yard or terminal**. This is the central classification for a road leg that feeds cargo into the rail network.

The key question is: **“Has the container been loaded at the customer/origin and is it now travelling into rail?”** If yes, it is BD. The customer/exporter is the *from* location and the rail yard/terminal is the *to* location.

| BD example | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| `D702837 20ft full from Laverton exporter to Dynon Rail Terminal` | `BD702837` — full collection to rail. |
| `D702837 40ft full from Dandenong packer to Melbourne rail yard` | `BD702837` — full container enters the rail network. |
| `D702837 full from Dynon Rail Terminal to Adelaide consignee` | **Not BD**; the container is leaving rail, so use DD for the road delivery leg and the applicable rail-linehaul PO for the rail segment. |

### 3.3 DD — Full Container Delivery: `DD[deal]`

Use **DD** when a **full** container is transported **from a rail yard, terminal, port, or designated handover point to the final delivery site**. It is the outbound road-delivery leg after the rail or terminal handover.

The key question is: **“Is the full container leaving the rail yard/terminal and being delivered to the consignee?”** If yes, it is DD. The rail yard or terminal is the *from* location and the customer/consignee is the *to* location.

| DD example | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| `D702837 20ft full from Adelaide Rail Terminal to Regency Park consignee` | `DD702837` — full delivery from rail to customer. |
| `D702837 40ft full from Melbourne terminal to Geelong delivery site` | `DD702837` — full container leaves terminal for the final destination. |
| `D702837 full from exporter to Dynon Rail Terminal` | **Not DD**; this is BD because the full container is travelling into rail. |

### 3.4 ED — Empty Dehire / Return: `ED[deal]`

Use **ED** after the container has been unpacked and is **empty**. The leg moves the empty container from the delivery/consignee side to the required dehire depot, empty return yard, or other nominated return facility.

The key question is: **“Has the container been emptied, and is this the return to the dehire or empty depot?”** If yes, it is ED. The delivery/unpacking location is the *from* location and the dehire depot is the *to* location. A rail yard should only be treated as the destination if it is specifically the instructed empty-return facility.

| ED example | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| `D702837 EMPTY 20ft from Regency Park consignee to Adelaide dehire depot` | `ED702837` — empty return after unpacking. |
| `D702837 EMPTY 40ft from Geelong customer to nominated empty return yard` | `ED702837` — empty dehire return. |
| `D702837 empty from Dynon yard to Laverton packing site` | **Not ED**; this is AD because the empty container is being delivered for loading. |

## 4. Rail-yard decision tree

Use this sequence before selecting the Vtiger cost line or checking the PO number.

1. **Is the container empty or full for this transport leg?** An empty container being sent to be loaded is different from an empty container being returned after unpacking.
2. **Is the rail yard/terminal at the beginning or end of the road leg?** A full container *to* rail is BD; a full container *from* rail is DD.
3. **If the container is empty, what is the operational purpose?** Empty *to the packer/origin* is AD. Empty *back from the consignee to dehire* is ED.
4. **Is the cost a rail line-haul charge instead of a road movement?** Use the relevant rail PO (P, SL, TR, or AZ), not AD/BD/DD/ED.
5. **Does the Vtiger Stage 1 cost field match the selected leg and contain a non-zero value?** The automation uses that field—not free-text route wording—to create the PO.

> **Quick rail-yard rule:** **Full container going *to* rail = BD. Full container coming *from* rail = DD. Empty container coming *from* an empty release point to be loaded = AD. Empty container going *to* its dehire/return facility = ED.**

## 5. Complete register of automated Stage 1 PO types

| Vtiger Stage 1 cost field | PO pattern for deal `D702837` | What it covers | Route or operational use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Empty Delivery | `AD702837` | Empty container delivery | Empty depot/yard to the origin, packer, or loading site. |
| Full Collection | `BD702837` | Full container collection | Origin/packer to rail yard, terminal, or line-haul handover point. |
| Full Container Delivery | `DD702837` | Full container delivery | Rail/terminal/handover point to consignee or final delivery site. |
| Empty Dehire | `ED702837` | Empty container return | Consignee/unpacking site to the nominated dehire or empty-return depot. |
| PN Rail Cost | `P702837` | Pacific National rail line-haul | Rail component; no inserted `D`. |
| Straitlink Bass Straight | `SL702837` | Straitlink/Bass Strait rail or line-haul cost | Rail/line-haul component; no inserted `D`. |
| Tasmanian Rail | `TR702837` | Tasmanian rail cost | Rail component; no inserted `D`. |
| Aurizon Rail | `AZ702837` | Aurizon rail cost | Rail component; no inserted `D`. |
| Hub Transfer | `TD702837` | First hub transfer | Transfer movement between nominated hubs or handling points. |
| Hub Transfer 2 | `TD702837-2` | Second hub transfer | Distinct second transfer for the same deal; the `-2` suffix prevents number collision. |
| Regional Connect | `RC702837` | Regional connection cost | Regional connecting transport/line-haul leg. |
| Transport to Storage | `JD702837` | Transport to storage | Movement to a storage facility. |
| Storage per Week | `GD702837` | Storage cost | Weekly storage charge; it is a cost PO rather than a physical road leg. |
| Insurance | `ID702837` | Insurance cost | Insurance charge associated with the deal. |

## 6. Worked multi-leg example

Assume deal **`D702837`** has the following operational movement: an empty container is released at an empty depot, delivered to the exporter, collected full and taken to the rail terminal, moved by rail, delivered full to the consignee, then returned empty to the dehire depot.

| Leg | Condition | Correct PO | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Empty release to exporter | Empty; depot/yard → origin | `AD702837` | The container is empty and is travelling to the loading site. |
| 2. Loaded exporter to rail terminal | Full; origin → rail yard | `BD702837` | The full container is travelling into rail. |
| 3. Rail line-haul | Rail cost | `P702837`, `SL702837`, `TR702837`, or `AZ702837` as applicable | This is the rail provider’s cost, not a road-leg prefix. |
| 4. Terminal to consignee | Full; rail yard → destination | `DD702837` | The full container is travelling out of rail to the customer. |
| 5. Consignee to empty-return depot | Empty; destination → dehire facility | `ED702837` | The container has been unpacked and is being returned empty. |

## 7. Checks before approving or querying a PO

Accounts staff should check that the PO prefix matches the actual leg shown on the supplier invoice or dispatch record. A mismatch between the route and the PO prefix should be queried before approval, especially where a supplier invoice refers to a rail terminal.

| Check | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Deal digits | Every PO should relate to the correct Vtiger deal, for example `702837`. |
| Empty vs full state | AD and ED are empty-container movements; BD and DD are full-container movements. |
| Direction relative to rail | BD is customer/origin → rail; DD is rail → customer/destination. |
| Amount | The amount supplied to the automation is GST-exclusive. |
| Duplicate protection | A PO already present in Xero should not be recreated automatically. |
| Multiple POs | More than one PO for a deal can be correct when more than one cost field has a non-zero amount. |

## 8. Exceptions and escalation

If a route does not fit these classifications, do not choose a prefix by guesswork. Check the actual Vtiger Stage 1 cost field and dispatch instruction. A full container movement between two non-rail hubs may be a **Hub Transfer** rather than BD or DD. A long-haul provider’s charge may be a rail PO rather than a road-leg PO.

If no PO appears after a Stage 1 transition, review the PO Requests screen. A webhook containing only the deal identifier, without any recognised transport-cost fields, cannot create a PO and will be shown as a failed workflow. The Vtiger webhook must include the applicable non-zero Stage 1 cost field(s) for the automation to create the required PO(s). [1]
